front.title: AGTP Presence: Ambient Discovery and Visibility for Agents

abstract.t:
This document specifies AGTP Presence, an ambient discovery and visibility layer for the Agent Transfer Protocol (AGTP). Existing agent discovery proposals are pull-based: an agent must know where to look (a catalog URL, a registry endpoint, a DNS name) before a query can begin. AGTP Presence inverts this model. When an agent joins the AGTP substrate, it becomes addressable and visible to the relevant scope of other agents immediately, without requiring registration with a central directory. In the vocabulary this family adopts from RFC 6763, Presence is the discovery layer: it resolves a known Canonical Agent-ID to the agent's current attachment. Search, which turns a capability need into candidate identities, is the DISCOVER method of the discovery companion; search runs over Presence.
The architecture combines three proven patterns: a Distributed Hash Table (DHT) keyed by Canonical Agent-ID for content-addressable routing, a gossip-based protocol for presence announcement and convergence, and trust-tier-scoped overlay partitioning for visibility control. Per-agent visibility is cryptographically declared in AGTP-CERT certificate extensions and enforced by the protocol, with three orthogonal axes of control: presence visibility, disclosure visibility, and audience scoping.
This document defines three new lifecycle methods (ANNOUNCE, WITHDRAW, PROBE), specifies the DHT and gossip protocols, defines the visibility model and its certificate extensions, addresses scaling through hybrid participation modes and federation-of-scoped-overlays, and provides a threat model with concrete mitigations.
